archetype: Mardu Vampire aristocrats on an eminence chassis — a go-wide token engine converted through eight sacrifice outlets into counters, cards and drain, with a lords-and-payoffs combat plan beside it. The frame (strategic_frame.json, this sha) agrees and names the same tension this diagnosis reports: the pilot's direction says the lifegain infinite is out, and the 99 still holds Bloodthirsty Conqueror with Vito and with Sanguine Bond, checker-passed as table kills (stacks 004, 006). That is reported here as a decision for the pilot, not made for him.
verdict: It develops as well as any deck in the quiver and closes worse than its board deserves. A castable Vampire in 95.0% of goldfish games at mean turn 2.22, a turn-three land drop 91.9% of the time, a draw engine in 83.5%, and both games logged on the current shape (004, 005) reached a dominant board and lost at the close — to a tutored infinite and to Purphoros pings. The measured kill routes are two one-card components (7.8% and 4.1% assembled, mean turns 6.4 and 6.7), the plan's payoff drain is a two-card pair at 37.2%, and the sweeper count is zero by role in a deck whose best logged turn was an opponent's wipe with a drain online. Colour is the cheap fix (black four sources short with a triple-pip card in the 99); the drain-and-sweeper layer is what costs games, and the Purphoros answer the pilot asked white for is a class (exile) the deck holds two of, plus — pending a stack — the Conqueror his direction marked as out.

open_questions.question: Bloodthirsty Conqueror, Vito (or Sanguine Bond) and Cruel Celebrant on the battlefield; one creature dies. Is the loop (stacks 004/006) already running, and can the pilot decline it? Same question with any lifelink hit or a Meathook trigger as the seed.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The pilot's direction says the lifegain infinite is OUT; the 99 holds it checker-passed twice. If the loop can be declined it is a play decision every turn those pieces coexist; if it cannot, 'out' is a list decision — cut Sanguine Bond or Conqueror — and that decision is the pilot's, not this diagnosis's. The answer also prices the Meathook add, which adds a trigger to the same loop.

open_questions.question: Tom's Purphoros triggers ('deals 2 damage to each opponent') with Bloodthirsty Conqueror on our battlefield: do Alex's and Oliver's life losses each fire Conqueror for us (net +2 per trigger), and with Vito or Sanguine Bond also out does each trigger drain Tom and start the loop?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If it reads as expected, the 99 already contains the strongest anti-Purphoros card the pilot could buy, and it is the one his direction has marked as out. That changes the 'is a white swap needed' answer from 'a third exile' to 'sequence Conqueror against Tom'.

open_questions.question: Boros Charm's 'permanents you control gain indestructible' with Elspeth, Storm Slayer attacked for lethal loyalty: does she survive? Which of the seven protection cards keep a planeswalker alive through (a) a destroy spell, (b) an exile spell, (c) combat damage?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The pilot asked whether the suite covers a walker. The doctor's oracle read is: Teferi's covers all three, Swat covers (a) and (b) when targeted, Boros Charm covers (a) only, and nothing but blockers covers (c). A stack settles it with rules citations before it becomes the pilot's habit.

open_questions.question: Re-run the goldfish with Ancient Tomb replaced by a Swamp (and Survivors' Encampment by Dragonskull Summit): commander mean cast turn (now 6.318, 60.3% by turn six), kill-by-turn-8 (now 0.704) and mean available mana by turn.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The painful cut is priced as a tempo loss nobody has measured. The goldfish cannot rank same-colour lands, but Tomb-to-Swamp is a colourless-for-black change it CAN see in castability, and the pilot should not sleeve a painful cut on a guess.

open_questions.question: Add the third death drain (Bastion of Remembrance, Zulaport Cutthroat or Vindictive Vampire) to the goldfish group 'A drain that fires when a creature DIES' and re-measure; and declare an outlet-AND-drain pair so the conversion layer has a rate at all.

open_questions.question: How does a mid-range aristocrats deck sequence against an each-opponent ETB-drain deck (Purphoros): attack it first, answer the enchantment, race on drain, or hold blockers? Is 'the natural predator for mid-range aggro' (log 005) a known matchup reading in the corpus?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The pilot's ask rests on one game. The corpus has racing, wrath-math and answer-economy sections but no matchup reading for a trigger-race opponent; the sequencing rule the pilot writes down next should come from a source, not a memory of one loss.

bracket_delta on every add is before 4 / after 4 because the floor is forced by the two contained two-card infinites, which no listed cut touches; if the pilot resolves the Conqueror decision by cutting Sanguine Bond or Conqueror, every delta must be recomputed with bracket-check.

Ancient Tomb's replacement is a fifth basic Swamp, and it cannot appear in add_candidates because the validator reads a basic the 99 already holds (Swamp ×4) as 'already in the maindeck'. The case, from mana_analysis on this sha: black is 32 sources against a Karsten target of 36 for 38 black cards and 54 black pips (Bloodletter is {1}{B}{B}{B}); black on curve is 0.785 on lands alone and 0.855 with rocks; a Swamp takes black to 33 (34 with Dragonskull Summit for Survivors' Encampment), enters untapped, deals no damage, and turns on Castle Locthwain, Dragonskull Summit, Blazemire Verge and Bleachbone Verge. Game Changers go 3 to 2 and the bracket floor stays 4 on the two infinites. The Ancient Tomb cut therefore has no paired add and is not applied by the validator's swap check; the goldfish open question above measures the tempo cost before anyone sleeves it.

findings.note: Dragonskull Summit for Survivors' Encampment is priced as 'Black 32 to 33 and red 20 to 21', and gaps[-1] says a Swamp plus Summit takes black to 34. mana_analysis.json (this sha) lands.list files Survivors' Encampment as produces ['B','R','W'], classes ['fixing','untapped-dual','utility'] — it is already inside the B 28 / R 17 / W 21 land counts the audit's colour-sources axis reads. By the artifact's own arithmetic the swap is B 32→32, R 20→20, W 24→23, and Swamp-for-Tomb plus Summit-for-Encampment is 33, not 34. The +1/+1 only holds under the doctor's oracle reading (axes[3]: 'Two lands add no colour without a cost') that Encampment is not a source — which is a fair reading of '{T}, Tap an untapped creature you control', and one mana_analysis's own assumption ('a source counts only for mana it produces unconditionally') arguably violates. That disagreement between oracle text and the measured artifact is the finding to name (agents-common §2); the diagnosis resolves it silently in its own favour and prices the 'cheapest axis to fix' with a gain the audit will not show when re-run. mana-fit does not list Encampment among its cut candidates either, which is consistent with it being credited as fixing.

threat-density is read as 'weakness' at a measured 10 against a floor of 3 on three legs, and two do not hold. (a) The one-card legs: deck-audit's own note says '2 declared target(s) rest on a component with one card… that is the ceiling on those lines, not a defect', and the 7.8% / 4.1% quoted as the one-card components' rates are the two-card LINE rates (Conqueror AND Vito-or-Bond; Bloodletter AND Sanctum Seeker per goldfish_targets 'need' groups) — the audit presents them the same way, but the verdict then reads a by-construction ceiling as a defect, which the charter names as over-claimed. (b) 'median first attack at global turn 12 and 13… 13… and 16': parse.py sets first_attack_turn = ev['turn'], the log's global turn counter (line 178/192/569). In a four-seat pod global turns 9–12 are round 3 and 13–16 round 4; in the five-seat pod 16 is round 4. The seat attacks on its third or fourth turn — early — and the figure is set beside goldfish own-turn means of 6.4–6.7 as though it were the same clock. (c) Logs 004 and 005 both have the deck reaching lethal ('closed the game before my lethal resolved'; 'pings finished the job before lethal landed') and losing to a tutored combo and a race — answer-economy and sequencing losses, which lean_into[3] itself says. The doctor's own enumeration of real closes (Bloodletter line, Conqueror loops, Akroma's Will alpha, Elenda) sits inside Zupke's 3–5. What the evidence reaches is 'adequate by count, fragile at the one-card legs, and the sweeper/drain layer is the measured gap' — which is what the prescriptions are actually sized off (sweepers 0, drain pair 0.372), so Meathook and a third drain survive this finding; the verdict sentence 'This is the axis that is costing games' does not. Alternatives tested: ramp 'adequate' is supported (land_drop t3 0.919, mean_available_mana t6 5.591, keep 0.811, no logged mana cause); colour-sources −4 is a real measured under, but its cheap fix is mis-priced (finding on add_candidates[3]).

Vish Kal's why leans on 'whose Forge seat's median first attack is global turn 12–13' as a clock that makes seven mana late; global turn 12–13 is the seat's third or fourth turn (see axes[9]). The evidence that does support the cut is in the artifacts the doctor already cites: engine_casts cast 0 / discarded 1 in n60 and absent in n40, and goldfish mean_available_mana_by_turn 7: 6.185, 8: 6.787, 9: 7.387 — seven mana is a turn-nine mean in the deck's own turns. Restate on those; the difficulty 'painful' and the cost_of_cutting are fair.

'the count is two or four depending on Tom's board' under-enumerates the devotion-five case. axes[6]'s count of two exile answers to a NONCREATURE Purphoros is correct (Anguished Unmaking; Despark, mv 4 — corpus oracle confirms {3}{R}). Once he is a creature, Path and Winds exile him AND Vish Kal's −1/−1-per-counter reduces toughness to 0, which is a state-based action (704.5f), not destruction, so indestructible does not apply; Liliana's −4 is a sacrifice, which indestructible also does not stop. Same omission in add_candidates[0]: Meathook at X≥5 removes a creature Purphoros too ('the Purphoros board, not Purphoros'). None of this changes the Vanishing Verse prescription, but the class the pilot needs is 'exile, toughness-reduction or sacrifice', and the deck holds more of it than 'two or four' says. (The doctor's expected answer on open_questions[2] is otherwise well-framed and correctly routed to resolve-stack.)

'eight sacrifice outlets (six free)': by oracle text seven of the eight cost no mana — Master of Dark Rites is '{T}, Sacrifice another creature: Add {B}{B}{B}', no mana in the cost — and strategic_frame.json on the same sha says 'seven of them cost no mana'. components[5].reading explains six as the goldfish group less Master (filed under mana), but `declared` states it as a fact about the 99 and disagrees with the frame; name the filing rather than restate the count. (engine.json's thesis says 'seven sacrifice outlets' — three artifacts, three counts; cards.json regex gives eight proper outlets plus High-Society Hunter's optional attack sacrifice and Reactor Raid's one-shot.)

'Thirteen Vampires at mana value two or less' / 'thirteen of them cost two or less and are the eminence leg': cards.json holds FOURTEEN Vampire creatures at cmc ≤ 2 — Viscera Seer ({B}, Vampire Wizard, the turn-one play in log 005) is not in the goldfish group, which was declared 2026-08-24 and repaired 2026-09-16 only by removing cut cards. The 95.0% / mean 2.22 is the declared thirteen's rate and is quoted correctly; the sentence states the count as the deck's. Say 'thirteen declared; cards.json has fourteen' and fold the missing card into open_questions[4]'s goldfish re-run.

'Bloodletter doubles it (damage is loss)': Bloodletter's clause is 'If an opponent would lose life DURING YOUR TURN' — a Vindictive Vampire trigger off an opponent's wipe (the log-002 scenario lean_into[0] is built on) is not doubled. Stack 007's whole result turns on that clause. Add the qualifier.

'The fastest opener in the 99' for Ancient Tomb: enumerated, Sol Ring is at least its equal (turn-one three mana with a land; log 003's four-mana turn one was two lands + Sol Ring + Talisman, no Tomb). Rhetorical, and the cut's substance (colourless in a 54-black-pip deck, 2 damage into a 'raced' loss, floor stays 4) is supported; drop the superlative or scope it.

Every strategy:* id fetched with lookup-strategy; every quote is verbatim. deckbuilding.ratios is quoted together with its own 'counts of functions' caveat and is not used as a rule — ramp and card-advantage are both read adequate against under counts, which is what the section asks for. interaction-suite ('one or two max', 'cover the classes', 'Depth is a meta call'), wrath-math ('assume the wrath', 'buy resilience'), threat-density, asymmetry, answer-economy, redundancy-vs-tutors, commander-insurance, pivot-window, metagame-clock, power-level, curve, archetype-selection, card-advantage and resource-hedging are each used within the sense of the whole section. The lean_into[0] argument that the deck should CAST the wipe is the doctor's own inference beyond wrath-math's text; asymmetry's 'preferring asymmetric board wipes' is the closer citation and is already attached.

Oracle text read for each: Meathook drains on our deaths and gains on theirs (the 'new trigger for the existing loop' note is right and correctly 'needs a stack scenario'); Bastion's token is created so Procession/Mondrak/Elspeth apply, and 13.7%→19.9% is the hypergeometric for 2→3 of 99 in seven; Vanishing Verse monocolored only; Summit checks Swamp/Mountain and the deck holds eight typed copies (Swamp ×4, Blood Crypt, Godless Shrine, Savai Triome, Smoldering Marsh); Zulaport; Toxic Deluge; Rakdos Charm's 'Exile target player's graveyard' matches deck_audit's breadth regex so it does close interaction-breadth.
